doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Top bands of 1939, Miller's pay and the Shribman brothers
summary: Top bands, theater scale and salaries, and Sy Shribman releasing Miller from a contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now in that year, was it 1939 is that right?
If there were four top bands in the country, especially considered — if the musicians considered the four top bands, who would they have been in 1939? The four top bands.
At that time? Who were they?
Who were the really hot bands at that time?
Well that’s when Miller actually came to the top. Shaw was still a hot band. Benny I guess had dropped some. I mean the swing bands. And of course you have Basie and Ellington, but they were always—
Always there. So when you got hired on to Glenn Miller, what kind of salary did he offer you?
Oh, it was a minimum thing I guess. I think it was $150 a week. I think.
Was that a salary so no matter how many nights you played, you got the same amount of money?

Well there was union scale for every job you play. There was a road scale for theaters and in those days it was $72 a week. You could play a hundred shows a week and you’d get $72. It wasn’t good. If you were a star of course, you could demand your salary. But the Miller band never really had any salaried, like Benny — Benny paid Harry James $500 a week when I was making $40 a week or something. And Ziggy Elman and Krupa. But they were making — Miller was in debt when he first started his success, and paid that off. Actually the Shribman brothers had a contract with Miller for 33-1/3 percent.

And I can remember Sy Shribman, when Miller made his, you know, was up, Shribman told Glenn he says, “That’s a lot of money, isn’t it Glenn?” You know he had a gravely voice. He says, “Well I’m going to let you out of that.” And he did. He let him off the hook.
That was pretty gentlemanly of him.
And that name comes up a lot.

Sy Shribman. Well Sy and Charlie and then another one, I can’t think of his name, a nephew, handled one of the big singers I can’t remember now but another Shribman. Out of Boston. Well they broke the Blue Devils. They were the ones — well we picked up Les Brown in Boston.
